newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS BEAT THE BLUES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS BEAT THE BLUES.

text.p: Mike Richter made 36 saves for his third straight win and Daniel Goneau and Niklas Sundstrom scored to lead the New York Rangers to a 2-1 victory over the St. Louis Blues Friday.
Wayne Gretzky set up the Rangers' second goal, digging out the puck in the left corner, skating behind the net and passing it to Sundstrom.

"Gretzky puts the puck where it needs to be," said Rangers coach Colin Campbell. "Gretzky causes a stir behind the net and it is tough to get him. It was an excellent play by him and we will see that often."
At New Jersey, Bobby Holik and Dave Andreychuk scored second-period goals to lift the New Jersey Devils into a 2-2 tie with the Ottawa Senators.
The Senators scored 47 seconds into the game as Shawn McEachern fired a slap shot from the left circl. Ottawa made it 2-0 five minutes later when rookie Andreas Dackell scored.
Holik put the Devils on the board at 2:40 of the middle period, and Andreychuk tied it at 19:35 with his first goal of the season.
In Phoenix, Scott Daniels had his first career two-goal game and Ron Hextall came within 1:56 of a shutout as the Philadelphia Flyers held off the Phoenix Coyotes, 3-1.
Daniels, who had just three goals in his first 66 NHL games, recorded the first two-point game of his career.
The Flyers went ahead 2-0 in the second period on Daniels' second goal.

In Washington, Dominik Hasek made 31 saves and Michal Grosek and Dixon Ward each had a goal and an assist in the third period, giving the Buffalo Sabres a 4-1 victory over the struggling Washington Capitals.
Hasek allowed only Richard Zednik's power-play goal with 4:57 left in the second period and turned away all nine shots in the third.
"I think we got embarrassed after we got beat by Tampa Bay a few days ago and we had to get back to the basics," Sabres coach Ted Nolan said.
At Anaheim, Chris Terreri turned aside 28 shots and Jeff Friesen had a goal and an assist as the San Jose Sharks scored three shorthanded tallies in a 4-1 defeat of the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim.
The Sharks, who also received a power-play tally from Owen Nolan, followed a scoreless first period with a pair of special-teams goals in each of the next two.
